412 I Tafseer as-Sa'di
Juz'30
The Prophet kept rising in status, and Allah supported the
religion with which He sent him and helped him against his enemies,
guiding him in all his affairs, until he died when he had attained a
level of favours, bliss, delight and joy that could not be attained by

except in this comprehensive phrase.

affairs:
c-jDid He not find you an orphan and take care of you?)? That is. He
found you without a mother or father; indeed his father and mother

care of him and caused his grandfather ‘Abdul-Muttalib to take care

Abu Talib to take care of him, until Allah supported him with His
help and with the believers.

you?}? That is. He found you not knowing anything about the scripture
or faith, and He taught you that which you did not know and enabled

c(Did He not find you in need)? that is, in poverty, t-jand make you
independent)? by means of what Allah enabled you to conquer of lands
from which wealth and taxes were brought to you.

(tawheed), even before his prophethood began, but he was unaware
of the path of Islam, and its rulings and teachings, until Allah guided

all other problems; you should respond with gratitude to the blessings

with the orphan, and do not feel impatient with him or scorn him;
rather you should honour him, give him what you can, and treat him
as you would like your child to be treated after you die.
«£and as for the beggar, do not speak harshly to him^ that is, do
not say anything to the beggar that may imply your rejection of his
request in a cruel or vicious manner; rather give him what you can,
or turn him away kindly.

includes those who ask for money and those who ask for knowledge.

reflects kindness towards the one who is striving to benefit the people

and worldly blessings
fjproclaim it» that is, praise Allah for it, and mention it in specific

his C ompanions abundantly until the Day of Judgement.
